source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Corn is sold either as fresh/wet cobs straight off the plant (ផ្លែពោតស្រស់) or as dried, shelled kernels (គ្រាប់ពោតស្អុត), and dried corn commands a materially higher price per kilogram because of the labor and drying cost already invested and lower spoilage risk. Prices below are in Cambodian riel per kilogram, from a 250-household survey covering the 2016-2017 season.

Wet corn cob prices by planting/harvest round: 1st-round harvest averaged 542 riel/kg (range 300-5,500); 2nd-round averaged 504 riel/kg (range 350-760); 3rd-round averaged 511 riel/kg (range 250-750).

Dried kernel prices by round: 1st-round averaged 751 riel/kg (range 400-950); 2nd-round averaged 780 riel/kg (range 700-880); 3rd-round averaged 729 riel/kg (range 480-860).

By province: wet corn averaged 706 riel/kg in Kampong Cham (range 330-5,500), 599 riel/kg in Kandal (range 470-740), 466 riel/kg in Battambang (range 370-700), and 383 riel/kg in Pailin (range 300-504). Dried kernels averaged 558 riel/kg in Kampong Cham (range 400-950), 792 riel/kg in Kandal (range 650-920), 732 riel/kg in Battambang (range 450-900), and 800 riel/kg in Pailin -- note the Pailin dried-kernel figure is based on a very small sample (only 0.4% of respondents, i.e. essentially one household), so the min/max/average are all identical (800) and this figure should be treated as low-confidence rather than a representative provincial price.

By year: wet corn averaged 622 riel/kg in 2014 (range 200-1,800), 549 riel/kg in 2015 (range 150-1,100), and 507 riel/kg in 2016 (range 100-900) -- showing a declining trend. Dried kernels averaged 927 riel/kg in 2014 (range 350-1,500), 858 riel/kg in 2015 (range 400-1,170), and 788 riel/kg in 2016 (range 400-1,100) -- also declining year over year.
